designs.title: Vineyard
designs.why: From 3 m it reads well: a strong arched vignette, clear depth from the grape leaves up to the farmhouse, and a clean heading and keyline. It earns its place on a white tee. Up close the art won't print as it is. The file is 1-bit, but all the tone is a single-pixel checkerboard/stochastic dither at 300 dpi: dots of about 0.085 mm, with roughly 13.5k isolated 1–2 px specks and about 10k 1–2 px open holes. On a 160–230 mesh on cotton, the highlight dots will wash out or fail to hold on the screen, so the distant hills, sky-side village and wall faces fade to nothing. The shadow gaps in the leaf canopy and terraces will fill in and turn into mud. Ink gain will make the mid-ground terraces heavier than the proof. The type, keyline and line work are fine.
designs.fix: Re-screen the tonal areas as a coarse AM halftone at about 45–55 lpi, 22.5°, round/elliptical dot. Clamp it at about 10% minimum and 85% maximum so no dot or gap is under about 0.15–0.2 mm (3+ px at 300 dpi), or convert the tone to engraved line hatching. Keep the keyline, title and outlines as solid vector line.
